title: Build an AI Real Estate App in 2026 (No Code Needed)
summary: Track properties, units, tenants, leases, repair requests and rent in one app you own. Three steps to build it, honest alternatives with prices, and limits.
body_markdown:
A property management app keeps properties, units, tenants, leases, repair requests and rent in one place, and reminds you before rent or a lease is due. This guide shows how to build one in Taskade Genesis without code, what it costs, four other ways to do it, and when dedicated property software is the better fit. To compare full property platforms side by side, read the guide to[AI property management software](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-property-management-software) .


> **TL;DR:** A property management app keeps properties, units, tenants, leases, repair requests and rent in one place, and reminds you before rent or a lease is due. Taskade Genesis builds it as one app with a tenant repair form, a rent ledger and reminders on a schedule. Pro is $10/month billed annually.[See plans and prices](https://www.taskade.com/pricing)


## Quick answer


To build a property management app without code, set up six lists: properties, units, tenants, leases, repair requests and rent payments. Then link each record to its unit and add reminders for rent and lease ends. TurboTenant is free if you also want online rent collection. Taskade Genesis builds the six lists as one app that you own and can change.


This guide is for small landlords, property managers and housing providers who run their portfolio from a spreadsheet and a phone today. If you are a real estate agent who needs a lead pipeline instead, read the[real estate CRM guide](https://www.taskade.com/blog/real-estate-crm) .


## What a property management app needs


A property management app needs six records, each linked to the unit it belongs to, and one reminder for each record that has a date. The table lists the key facts to keep for each record and the reminder that goes with it. Start with these facts and add more only when a real question needs them.


Record Key facts Reminder


Property Address, owner, insurance renewal date Insurance renewal, 30 days before


Unit Unit number, bedrooms, rent amount, status (let, empty, being repaired) None


Tenant Name, email, phone, emergency contact None


Lease Unit, tenant, start date, end date, deposit amount Renewal check, 60 days before the end


Rent payment Unit, month, amount, due date, paid date Due date, and a late notice if unpaid


Repair request Unit, what is wrong, urgency, contractor, cost Assigned contractor, and done


The picture shows how the records hang together. Every record points to a unit, and every unit points to a property. That is why one search for a unit shows its tenant, its lease, its rent and its repairs.


```text
PROPERTY  14 Oak Street (owner, insurance date)
|
+-- UNIT 1A  (2 bed, $1,450/month, let)
|      |
|      +-- TENANT   J. Rivera (email, phone)
|      +-- LEASE    2026-02-01 to 2027-01-31, deposit $1,450
|      +-- RENT     Oct: paid 10-01 | Nov: due 11-01
|      +-- REPAIRS  Leaking tap: done, $85 | Heater: assigned
|
+-- UNIT 1B  (1 bed, $1,100/month, empty)
|
+-- REPAIRS  Repaint before letting: open


```


## How the records link together


The six records form one small database. A property holds many units. A unit holds many leases over time, many rent payments and many repair requests. A tenant can hold more than one lease. The diagram shows the links that the app needs, so that each screen can show everything about one unit.


A repair request moves in one direction: the tenant sends it, the app sorts it, a contractor gets it, and the cost lands next to the unit. The diagram shows the path for one request.


## Build it in Taskade in 3 steps


To build the property management app in Taskade, describe it to Taskade EVE, load your units and tenants, then turn on the rent, lease and repair reminders. A landlord with a spreadsheet of units can have a working app the same day. Each step below says which plan it needs.

The link opens Create with this prompt filled in. Edit it to match your portfolio, then send it. Building the app uses[AI credits](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/model-credits) .


```text
Build a property management app for a small landlord. Lists:
properties, units, tenants, leases, rent payments and repair requests.
Link each unit to its property, each lease to a unit and a tenant, and
```

### Step 2: Load your units and tenants, and share the repair form


Most landlords already keep their units and tenants in a spreadsheet. Save each tab as a CSV file and import each one into its project with the[CSV import guide](https://www.taskade.com/learn/import/csv-import) . A CSV file can be up to 5 MB on every plan, including Free.


Spreadsheet tab Columns to keep Import into


Properties Address, owner, insurance renewal date Properties


Units Property, unit number, bedrooms, rent amount, status Units


Tenants Name, email, phone, unit, lease start, lease end, deposit Tenants and Leases


Rent Unit, month, amount, due date, paid date Rent ledger


Next, share the repair form with your tenants. A form like the one below sends each request straight into the Repairs project, linked to the unit. The[form with logic guide](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/build-form-with-logic) shows how to ask a follow-up question only when it matters, for example "Is water leaking now?"


Tenants and contractors can sign in to the app on every plan, Free included. Sign-in confirms who each person is. To show each tenant only their own lease and repairs, match each lease to the tenant's email and test it with a second account before you share the link. Do the same for contractors with the repair requests. The[App Users guide](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/app-users) covers the settings, and app users do not take a workspace seat.


### Step 3: Turn on rent, lease and repair reminders


The app runs on four automations. Each one uses built-in Taskade steps, so all four run on every plan. Open **Automations** in the app and check or set them up as the table shows.


Automation Starts when Steps Plan


1. Rent due A rent row's due date arrives ([Task Due](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/task-due) ) Email the tenant, and assign the row to you Every plan


2. Lease renewal A renewal check's due date arrives, 60 days before the lease ends Assign the check to you and email you the lease Every plan


3. Repair request A repair form is sent ([AI Forms](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/forms-trigger) ) Categorize with AI (emergency or routine), assign the contractor, email them Every plan (the AI step uses AI credits)


4. Monthly summary The 1st of each month at 08:00 ([Schedule](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/schedule) ) Find rent rows and open repairs, email you the summary Every plan


The rent automation fires on the due date. For a heads-up 3 days earlier, add a[reminder](https://www.taskade.com/learn/projects/reminders) to the rent row, which notifies you on your phone or desktop. For lease ends, add a renewal check task with a due date 60 days before each lease ends. Taskade EVE can add those tasks for every lease in one step if you ask.


Test the setup with one unit before you use it for the whole portfolio. Send a test repair request as a tenant, set a test rent row due today, and set the monthly summary to run once a few minutes from now. Then set it back to the 1st. You are done when the contractor email, the rent email and the summary all arrive.


A UK supported-housing provider runs its whole back office in one Taskade Genesis app: properties, landlords, tenants, bookings, compliance checks, repairs, invoices and rent reconciliation, across 19 data tables.


## Add inspections, lease files and late fees


Three jobs come next once the six records work: inspections at move-in and move-out, the signed lease file, and a late fee when rent stays unpaid. Each one is a field or a small project on the unit, plus one automation. Add them one at a time, after the first month runs clean.


Job What you add How it runs


Move-in and move-out inspection An Inspections project: unit, date, room-by-room checklist, photos The tenant or you fill the checklist on a phone, and photos attach to each room


Lease file A file field on the lease record Attach the signed PDF. An AI agent with the leases in its knowledge answers "when can the tenant at 1A give notice?"


Late fee A Late fee field on the rent row A daily check finds unpaid rows 5 days past the due date, adds the fee you set and emails the tenant


Costs per property A Cost field on each repair The monthly summary adds rent in and repair costs out for each property


Compare the move-out inspection with the move-in one, room by room, before you return a deposit. The photos with dates on both rows answer most deposit questions. Check the late fee rules in your area before you set the amount, because many places cap it.

## For real estate agents: AI apps for leads, showings and closings


An AI real estate app for an agent does a different job from a property manager: it captures leads, answers them fast, books showings and keeps each deal on a checklist to closing. A no-code AI agent can also do property listing research: it reads the listing pages and documents you give it and drafts a summary for the client. The same Taskade Genesis parts handle it. Follow up fast A new inquiry gets a reply and qualifying questions on budget, timeline and area[How to automate real estate work](https://www.taskade.com/blog/automate-real-estate)

Run the closing One checklist for inspection, appraisal and financing dates[Closing checklist portal](https://www.taskade.com/blog/closing-checklist-portal)


Five follow-up automations cover most of an agent's routine. Each one is a trigger plus a few steps:


1. **New inquiry reply.** A landing-page form starts the automation, an AI step drafts a reply with qualifying questions, and you send it or let it go out.
2. **Showing reminders.** A due date on each showing sends the buyer the address the day before and asks for feedback after.
3. **Long-term nurture.** A weekly schedule emails buyers who are not ready yet with new listings that match their criteria.
4. **After the closing.** A date 7 days after the closing asks for a review, and a date one year later sends an anniversary note.
5. **Commission log.** When a deal's status changes to Closed, the automation adds the deal and the commission to a finance project.

## Limitations: when Taskade is not the right fit


Choose dedicated property software when you need to collect rent online, hold deposits, screen tenants, run trust accounting or send year-end tax forms. Taskade runs the records, the repair requests and the reminders around those jobs. These are the limits to know before you build:


- **No online rent collection or deposit accounting.** There is no QuickBooks or Xero connector. Keep your bookkeeping tool for the money, and record paid dates in the app.
- **No tenant screening or credit checks.** Use a screening service, then add the tenant to the app.
- **No listing syndication.** The app does not post empty units to rental listing sites.
- **No e-signature for leases.** Sign leases in an e-signature tool and attach the file to the lease record.
- **AI sorting of repairs uses AI credits.** The built-in reminders and emails do not.


## FAQ


Can I build a property management app without code?


Yes. A property management app needs six linked lists: properties, units, tenants, leases, repair requests and rent payments, plus reminders for rent and lease ends. Taskade Genesis builds the six lists as one app from a plain-language description. You load your units from a spreadsheet, share a repair form with tenants, and turn on the reminders.


Can tenants send repair requests?


Yes. Share the app's repair form with tenants. Each request becomes a record linked to the unit, an AI step can mark it as an emergency or routine, and an automation assigns it to a contractor and emails them. The tenant gets an email when the repair is done.


Can tenants sign in and see their own lease?


Yes. App sign-in works on every plan, Free included. Sign-in confirms who each tenant is. To show each tenant only their own lease and repair requests, match each lease to the tenant's email, and test it with a second account before you share the link.


Does it remind me when rent or a lease is due?


Yes. Give each rent payment a due date, and a Task Due automation emails the tenant and you when the date arrives. For lease ends, add a renewal check with a due date 60 days before the lease ends. Built-in reminders and emails run on every plan.


Can I import my current spreadsheet?


Yes. Save each tab of your spreadsheet as a CSV file, one for properties, one for units and one for tenants, and import each file into its project. A CSV file can be up to 5 MB on every plan, including Free.


Can a contractor see only the jobs assigned to them?


Yes, with the same setup as tenants. A contractor signs in to the app, and sign-in confirms who they are. Match each repair request to the contractor's email, and test it with a second account. Each contractor then works from their own list.


How much does a property management app cost in Taskade?


Free covers 2 members, 3 apps and 10 automation runs a month, and it starts with no AI credits, so it fits a trial with a few units. Pro is $10 a month billed annually ($20 monthly) for up to 10 members, with 1,000 automation runs a month. Taskade does not charge per unit.


What is the best AI app for real estate agents?


The best AI app for a real estate agent does four jobs: it captures leads, replies to them fast, books showings and keeps each deal on a checklist to closing. In Taskade Genesis you start from the Real Estate Landing Page, the Broker Calendar and the Neon CRM Dashboard apps, then add follow-up automations. Dedicated agent CRMs fit teams that need MLS feeds.


Can I track move-in and move-out inspections?


Yes. Add an Inspections project with the unit, the date and a checklist for each room, and attach photos to each item from a phone. Compare the move-out inspection with the move-in one before you return a deposit. Taskade EVE can add the project and the checklist in one step if you ask.


When is TurboTenant, Stessa or Buildium the better choice?


Pick dedicated property software when you need online rent collection, tenant screening, deposits, trust accounting or year-end tax forms. TurboTenant has a free plan, Stessa Manage is $12 a month paid annually, and Buildium Essential starts at $62 a month.
